clue.text: Comic character fools about

indicators.note: about signals that the word for the fools is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool, and two of them make NIT NIT

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure clowns around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NITNIT (two nits for 'fools') round. Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's Belgian comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé's young reporter is the hero of a famous Belgian comic strip, so he is a comic character.

clue.text: Like schoolmasters, they care about inspiring learner

indicators.note: inspiring in its sense of breathing in, so the rearranged letters take in another
about means the letters of they care are moved around

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Schoolmasters are caring people who motivate their pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THEY CARE to TEACHERY, and 'inspiring' breathes L in.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacherly describes the manner of someone who teaches, as schoolmasters do.

clue.text: Boat builder hasn't finished installing room for woman

indicators.note: installing means the builder's name takes in the room abbreviation
not finished means the final letter of the name is cut

parts.note: Noah built the ark

explanation.surface: A shipwright without completing the job fits out a cabin for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' drops the final letter of the ark-builder's name; 'installing' sets the room letters in what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female forename, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Suggesting I'm being deceitful if put under pressure

indicators.note: put under places the deceit word beneath the pressure letter in this down clue

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
lying is being deceitful

explanation.surface: Insinuating that I'm telling lies when squeezed.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest without saying outright, so implying is suggesting.

clue.text: Creature first to enter snare is grabbed by fox

indicators.note: being grabbed by the fox word means sitting inside it

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the word enter

parts.note: a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: An animal walks into a trap and is seized by a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to' takes only the opening letter of 'enter'; tod is an old Scots and northern word for a fox, and 'is grabbed by' puts the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-footed vertebrate is called a tetrapod, so any such animal is a creature of that kind.

clue.text: Art movement, say, leading to rise of vice in island

indicators.note: leading to puts the speaking word in front of the rest

parts.note: to express is to say

indicators.note: in places the turned vice word inside the island abbreviation

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue means the vice word is read upwards

parts.note: a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: An artistic school, for example, leading to more depravity on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reads the vice word upwards, and 'in' sets it inside the Isle of Man abbreviation, giving IONISM; 'say' looks like an example marker but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressionism was an early 20th-century artistic movement distorting reality to convey emotion.

clue.text: Watch anger rising, in a way

indicators.note: in places the turned anger word within the road abbreviation

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the anger word is read upwards

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Observe fury building up, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it attentively, to watch it.

clue.text: Measure of energy put into bars by one composer

indicators.note: put into means the energy unit goes inside the bars word

parts.note: poles are bars or rods
the erg is a unit of energy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A unit of energy is spent in pubs by a single musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an 18th-century Italian who wrote the Stabat Mater, so a composer.

clue.text: Make fruit cake, American-style

parts.note: to do is to make or produce
a nut is a hard-shelled fruit

explanation.surface: Bake a fruitcake the way they do in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Donut is the US spelling of doughnut, a ring of fried sweet dough, so an American cake.

clue.text: Powerful Roman with firm hold on a state

parts.note: a firm hold is a grip
PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state

explanation.surface: A mighty Roman keeps a tight grip on a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's general and right-hand man, one of the most powerful men in Rome.

clue.text: Feature in Paris Match re period during revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A French magazine reports on a time of revolutionary upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French news magazine; 'during revolution' rearranges MATCH RE PERIOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The great triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées is a landmark of the French capital.

clue.text: Metal clasp holding together old dress seen from the back

indicators.note: a pin holding something together has it gripped between its parts, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pin is a simple clasp or fastener

indicators.note: seen from the back means the words old and dress are read from their far end

parts.note: to rig out is to dress, so rig means dress or outfit

explanation.surface: A brooch fastens an antique gown, viewed from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from the back' reverses old-plus-dress into GIRO; 'holding together' puts that inside the clasp, after its I. 'Metal' looks like part of the clasp but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude iron straight from the blast furnace, cast in bars, is a metal.

clue.text: Male meets topless female that's exciting

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male

indicators.note: topless means the word for the female loses its first letter

parts.note: a lady is a female

explanation.surface: A man encounters a woman without a top, which is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes L off LADY to leave ADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heady is intoxicating or exhilarating, which is to say it excites.

clue.text: Tidies leaves

definitions.meaning: empties a cupboard or room of unwanted things
goes away, departs, often in a hurry

explanation.definitionFit: To clear out a room is to tidy it by emptying it; to clear out is also slang for to depart.

clue.text: Teller of tales broadcast once as true

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A storyteller on the radio was once regarded as truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the ten letters of ONCE AS TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteuse is a woman skilled at telling anecdotes, a female storyteller.

clue.text: In Winnie's place, there's little time to spring clean for a start

indicators.note: for a start puts the cleaning word at the front, before the other pieces

parts.note: to char is to clean houses for a living
T is the abbreviation for time
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: At Churchill's house there's a brief chance to do spring cleaning first.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie is Winston Churchill; Chartwell is his country house in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartwell in Kent was Winston Churchill's family home for forty years, so it is his place.

clue.text: One with starring role is shot

definitions.meaning: the principal actor in a play or film
pellets of the heavy metal fired from a shotgun

explanation.definitionFit: The lead is the main part or its actor; shot is made of lead, the soft heavy metal.

clue.text: One's found party dead

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
dead as in dead easy means very

explanation.surface: Someone at a party has been found dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, a thing that has been uncovered.

clue.text: Speaker's one who'll succeed, having natural ability as a high-flyer?

indicators.note: a speaker's version means the words are as they sound when said

parts.words: one who'll succeed, having natural ability
parts.note: an heir is one who will succeed to a title or estate; someone born to a skill has natural ability, as in a born leader

explanation.surface: A successor with innate talent is hailed as a rising star.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is aloft in flight, as a high-flyer literally is.

clue.text: Group of students finally pay attention

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word pay

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: In the end, students must listen carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year is a cohort of pupils of the same age, taught as one group.

clue.text: Main requirements in religious institutions, it appears

indicators.note: in places the word it inside the word for the religious houses

parts.note: priories are houses of monks or nuns

explanation.surface: The basic needs of monasteries, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Priorities are the things that matter most, the chief needs to be dealt with first.

clue.text: Cloth spun in Aragon

indicators.note: spun as yarn is twisted, so the letters of the region are twisted round

explanation.surface: Fabric woven in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: Aragon is a region of north-eastern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a fabric made from the soft hair of the Angora goat or rabbit.

clue.text: Italian film director not in favour of screening tear-jerker

indicators.note: screening means covering or hiding, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: to be anti something is to oppose it
chopping an onion makes the eyes water, a playful tear-jerker

explanation.surface: An Italian filmmaker opposed to showing a weepie.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo Antonioni made L'Avventura and Blow-Up, so he is an Italian film director.

clue.text: Province formerly covered by Italian journalist

indicators.note: covered by means the letters lie concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A former region reported on by an Italian reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a province of old France around Angers, abolished with the Revolution.

clue.text: Fail to show support, perhaps, for party

definitions.meaning: split as ..., to cast a vote against, which is one way of not supporting

explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British slang for a festive party; split three ways it reads as being a vote against.

clue.text: Rather like odd slices of cake, unfortunately

parts.note: à la means in the manner of, rather like

indicators.note: odd slices are the first and third letters of the word cake

explanation.surface: Sadly, much like the uneven pieces of a gateau.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old exclamation of sorrow or regret, meaning alas.

clue.text: Fellow heartlessly gags pensioner

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the word for gags is cut out

parts.note: gags are jokes
OAP is old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: A man cruelly makes jokes about an old-age pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes K, the central letter, from JOKES. Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary bloke, often a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is British slang for an average man, so the phrase is another word for a chap or fellow.

clue.text: Springtime holiday home in France I swapped for a place in England

parts.note: Mar is the short form of March, a spring month

indicators.note: swapped for says the letter I is exchanged for the letter A in the French cottage word

parts.note: a gîte is a French holiday cottage

explanation.surface: A spring break in a French cottage gets exchanged for a trip to England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapped for' turns GITE into GATE. Margate is a seaside resort in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a seaside town on the Kent coast, so it is a place in England.

clue.text: Having discharged gun, gangster leader making off with lots of money

indicators.note: the leader making off means the first letter of the gangster word departs

parts.note: a gun, or hired gun, is a gunman or gangster
loaded is slang for having lots of money

explanation.surface: After firing, the gang boss runs off with a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader making off' removes G from GUN, leaving UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm that has fired off its rounds or had them removed is no longer charged, so it is empty.

clue.text: Periodical we see displayed round front of kiosk

indicators.note: round means the bishop's seat word goes around the next letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

indicators.note: front of points at the opening letter of the word kiosk

explanation.surface: A magazine we spot on show around the newsstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives K, which 'round' puts inside ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekly is a magazine or paper published every seven days, a kind of periodical.
